- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 1–3% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to overcorrect downward; if below, overcorrects upward — apply opposite bias correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment shifts sharply, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment direction.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
